steps.what: Obtain actual patient histories and clarify complaints, illnesses and psychosocial context
Enter and verify identifying data and actual prior-history references
outputs: verified patient identity and history references

steps.what: Write the actual patient history in the clinical record system {OTHER}
inputs: verified patient identity and history references

loop.purpose: Draft a patient history note from actual captured history
loop.input: Practitioner-captured patient account and verified prior-history references
loop.check: Practitioner checks patient identity, negation, chronology, omitted complaints and family or psychosocial meaning against actual history
loop.stop: Missing actual history or two failed corrections returns note writing to the practitioner
loop.why_not_simpler: Native identity fields and fixed history headings come first; variable patient narrative needs bounded drafting

steps.what: Check the final patient history note and exact patient record destination
Commit the checked final patient history note

tasks.design: Reuse verified identity and prior-record references in the clinical record system {OTHER}, then use a bounded note draft from actual captured history. The practitioner still obtains and clarifies the history, captures source information, corrects the narrative and checks its exact final patient destination before committing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identity fields and narrative history can require repeated entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient references and bounded clinical-note drafting can reduce repeated fields and first-draft writing.
tasks.still_hard: Clarifying sensitive history and distinguishing a patient's account from an established clinical fact require care and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner notices ambiguity and asks the patient rather than filling a plausible gap.
tasks.altitude: Less history-note drafting; clinical responsibility and decision rights stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records for clinician validation; this supports note assistance, not diagnosis or a measured saving for naturopathic practice.

assumptions: Boundary is actual history documentation through its checked saved note, including obtaining actual source history. No diagnosis or treatment selection is automated.

The patient provides actual complaints and history in s1; the record supplies actual patient identifier and available prior sources. The practitioner verifies identity in s2 and captures history by actual note entry or dictation in s3. Capture, correction and unsupported source entry remain in s3 retained time; no free transcript is assumed.

Test native identity fields and history templates before custom code. Existing identity reuse earns no saving. Access, appropriate patient information and recording permission where required must match actual practice; the design can use practitioner dictation without recording the consultation.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. The final commit is one percent fully retained; s4 is the existing final note check.
unknowns: What history entry is still repeated?
Does the actual record support note assistance and appropriate access?
research_questions: Does assisted documentation reduce time after all source capture, correction and final checking are counted?

already_counted.description: Capture history and correct narrative meaning within s3.

incremental.description: Maintain note mappings and audit omissions after updates.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final patient history note and exact patient record destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.50 repeated identity fields + 49*0.40 narrative = 24.6; minus 1.5 upkeep = 23.1. If half of fields and narrative are eligible, 12.3 minus 1.5 = 10.8. History conversation and final commit remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find and assess actual patient education material for the healthcare management question
Educate patients about health care management and check actual understanding
outputs: actual education discussion and understanding observations

steps.what: Write and check the actual patient education record
inputs: actual education discussion and understanding observations

steps.what: Save the checked actual patient education record

tasks.design: Configure approved material filters in {DOCS} and reuse selected source references in the clinical record system {OTHER}. The practitioner assesses relevance, teaches the patient, checks understanding and captures the actual discussion; no model gives personalised health advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant approved page and repeating its reference can interrupt education.
tasks.enabler_now: Native material filters and linked record fields can reduce lookup and repeated metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Patient understanding, personal relevance and health-management decisions need a practitioner.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner responds to misunderstanding and recognises when the patient needs a different explanation or care route.
tasks.altitude: Less material lookup; patient education responsibility stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: approved education-library filters and linked record references can reduce lookup and repeated metadata without giving personal advice.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual patient education and its existing record. No new handout send or report is added where actual practice does not use one.

Education-content owner supplies actual topic, version and source location; patient supplies actual questions. The practitioner assesses relevance in s1 and records actual education and understanding in s3 after s2. Missing metadata and unsupported records stay manual; understanding is never inferred from material availability.
Test native filters and linked fields before code. Existing lookup configuration earns no saving. Only reference and context repetition changes in s3; actual patient observations remain manual.
Shares are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. The same-system save is one percent fully retained and the existing note check supplies its gate.
unknowns: Which approved sources are used today?
What education documentation is actually required and written?
research_questions: Can native lookup reduce source finding without reducing time teaching or checking understanding?

incremental.description: Maintain education filters and source-reference fields.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final patient education record and exact patient destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.40 lookup + 9*0.20 repeated references = 5.8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 5.3. With half the lookup and fields eligible, 2.9 minus 0.5 = 2.4. Patient education and save time stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.design: Configure native patient-context and approved reference views in the clinical record system {OTHER}. The practitioner assesses suitability and gives advice personally; linked identity and reference fields reduce repetition in the actual advice record without selecting a regimen.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice can require finding patient context and repeating source references in the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and linked note fields can reduce retrieval and metadata repetition.
tasks.still_hard: Appropriateness, contraindications, patient goals and the limits of evidence need clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner recognises when the patient's circumstances require different care or further assessment.
tasks.altitude: Less reference handling; clinical advice authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical-record views and reference fields can reduce information retrieval and repeated metadata; they do not establish a suitable therapeutic regimen.

assumptions: Boundary is actual advice and its existing clinical record, without an added follow-up report. Patient assessment and advice selection remain human and within actual practitioner scope.

Patient and record supply actual identity, concerns and history; reference owner supplies actual source topic and revision. The practitioner verifies relevance in s1-s2 and captures actual discussion in s4. Missing patient context or references stay manual; no structured clinical advice is assumed free.

Test native views and fields before code. Existing context retrieval earns no saving. Only source finding and repeated identity/reference fields change, not clinical reading, decisions or conversation.
Shares are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Final save has one percent fully retained time and uses the existing record check.
unknowns: What context retrieval is already automatic?
What advice and documentation lie within the practitioner's actual scope?
research_questions: Does native context reuse save time while retaining all suitability and patient-understanding work?

incremental.description: Maintain advice-reference views and note-field mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.40 retrieval + 9*0.20 repeated fields = 5.8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 5.3. If half the source finding and fields qualify, 2.9 minus 0.5 = 2.4. All clinical choices and advice remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer, dispense or prescribe natural medicines within actual scope.

steps.what: Review actual patient history, medicines, allergies and applicable treatment information
inputs: actual current medicine and supplement list

steps.what: Decide whether and which natural medicine is appropriate within actual authorised scope
Enter the actual product, patient, amount and treatment instruction
Check the final patient-specific instruction, product, route and actual action destination
Send the checked prescription or dispensing instruction to its actual recipient
Actually administer or dispense the authorised product and observe the patient
Write and check actual medicine prescription, administration or dispensing outcomes
Commit the checked actual treatment record to the patient record

tasks.design: Configure native patient and product reference fields in the clinical record system {OTHER} to reduce repeated instruction entry. Treatment selection, checks, sending, actual administration or dispensing and recording actual outcomes stay with the authorised practitioner; no model selects or prescribes a medicine.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual treatment instructions can repeat patient and product identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue and patient links can reuse verified identifier fields.
tasks.still_hard: Suitability, interactions, evidence, patient response and actual prescribing or dispensing authority require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner recognises when treatment is inappropriate or requires a different authorised clinician.
tasks.altitude: Less identifier re-entry; treatment rights remain exactly as actually authorised.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical systems may reuse verified patient and catalogue identifiers in treatment instructions; this does not establish product efficacy or practitioner prescribing rights.

assumptions: Prescribing, dispensing and administering are alternative activity branches. Shares describe a provisional workload mix, not every action on every patient. Reweight to actual authorised practice; prescription-only cases use actual prescription outcome and never invent administration. Physical-only cases omit a nonexistent send and reweight.

No prescribing or dispensing right follows from the occupation title. Verify actual practitioner credentials, national rules, product status and clinical-system permissions before enabling an action; otherwise retain the actual referral to an authorised practitioner, with no transferred labour saving claimed.

Patient record provides actual identity and current medicines; product catalogue owner provides actual product identifier, form and strength where available. The practitioner chooses and enters actual amount, route and schedule in s2-s3, checks the exact instruction in s4 and captures actual outcomes only after the relevant action. Missing or unsuitable catalogue fields stay manual; no structured outcome is assumed free.

Test native reference fields before code. Existing catalogue population and medication-check runtime earn no saving. Only repeated identifiers in s3 change; all clinical decisions, source reading, physical work and outcome writing remain unchanged.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Routine send and record commit retain their one percent shares; exact instruction checking is existing treatment work.
unknowns: What actions lie within the actual practitioner's national scope?
Which products have reliable catalogue fields?
What is the actual prescribe, dispense and administer mix?
research_questions: Is any identifier entry repeated after accounting for existing native patient and product links?

incremental.description: Maintain patient/product reference configuration and check catalogue changes.
